questions.q: What is a vision-language model, more precisely than 'a model that can see'?
options: A text model paired with a separate image-classification plugin
A single model trained so images and text share the same underlying reasoning space
A model that can only caption images, never reason about them
A model that converts images into text before any reasoning happens
questions.explain: A VLM is one model trained jointly over images and text, not a text model bolted to a separate image tool — that's why it can reason about a chart, not just describe it.

questions.q: In Claude's Messages API, what are the three supported source types for an image content block?
options: base64, url, and file_id
jpeg, png, and gif only
local, remote, and cached
text, image, and audio
questions.explain: An image's source object can be base64 (embedded bytes), url (a hosted link), or file_id (a one-time Files API upload referenced by id).

questions.q: What determines the 'visual token' cost of an image sent to Claude?
options: The file name of the image
The number of colors in the image
The image's resolution, broken into 28x28-pixel patches
Whether the image is a screenshot or a photo
questions.explain: Claude costs images per 28x28-pixel patch — resolution directly drives token cost, the same way word count drives text token cost.

questions.q: According to documented vision-model limitations covered in this lesson, which task should you NOT trust a current vision-language model to do reliably?
options: Reading a bar chart's general trend
Detecting whether an image itself was AI-generated
Describing the general contents of a clear, high-quality photo
Reading large, legible text in a well-lit image
questions.explain: No current vision-language model can reliably detect whether an image was AI-generated — this is an explicitly documented limitation, not an edge case.

questions.q: Why would an application upload a frequently reused image via the Files API instead of resending it as base64 on every turn?
options: The Files API is the only way to send images larger than 1MB
base64 images cannot be used in multi-turn conversations at all
Files API images do not count toward visual token cost
It avoids re-sending the full image bytes on every turn, keeping request payloads smaller as the conversation grows
questions.explain: Uploading once and referencing by file_id keeps payloads small across turns; re-sending base64 data resends the full image bytes every single turn.
